hypothesis: Names breaking their first 15-minute high on heavy relative volume keep going into the late morning. Written before any run; the published version of this idea reports a gross edge, so the question is whether it survives spread and slippage.
name: Opening-range breakout, stocks in play

hypothesis: A liquid large cap that opens more than 1% below yesterday's close, in a thin pre-market after overnight order imbalance, retraces part of that gap during the first two hours as the regular session's deeper liquidity arrives. The cost is a fixed few bps while a 1%+ gap leaves far more room to be recovered, so net-of-cost edge is plausible where it was not for breakouts. Written before any run. If the gap-ups and gap-downs that carry real news dominate, this loses and the stop (1.5%) is what limits it.
name: Gap-down fade, large caps

hypothesis: Execution desks benchmarked to VWAP buy when a stock trades well under it, pulling price back toward VWAP later in the day. Costs are fixed in bps, so only a deep (1.2%) stretch below VWAP, after the first hour, leaves enough expected reversion to clear them; shallow stretches (the usual setting) cannot. The target is about the size of the stretch. Written before any run. Expected to fail if a stock far below VWAP is mostly a stock with news, which trends rather than reverts.
name: VWAP reversion, deep stretches only
